titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 18, the tribunals, sections A–E
work: Book of the Dead of Ani
workEn: Book of the Dead of Ani
draftNote: Draft — the hieroglyphs are read from the printed type of Budge's 1895 edition of the papyrus, and the signs and readings are still being checked; expect changes.
source: Papyrus of Ani (British Museum EA 10470), Plate XIII. Hieroglyphs transcribed from the interlinear text of E. A. W. Budge, The Book of the Dead: The Papyrus of Ani in the British Museum (London, 1895), pp. 75–78; Budge's transliteration and word-by-word English were used to check the reading of the signs and the sense, never for wording. Only the papyrus's own text is given: the passages Budge supplies from other papyri in his appendixes and footnotes are left out. Transliteration in the Leiden convention, with the reed written i; translation made fresh from the Egyptian. Shown left to right; the papyrus is written in columns read from the top down. The line under each word ("say") is the conventional Egyptological classroom pronunciation — a neutral e between consonants; ꜣ and ꜥ as a; w as u or w; ṯ as tj; ḏ as dj; ḫ and ẖ as kh; š as sh — an artificial teaching pronunciation, since the vowels of Egyptian were never written. The grouping of signs within a word follows Budge's type, which regularises the scribe's hand.
about: Spell 18 proper begins on Plate 13 of Ani's papyrus, after its introduction on Plate 12. In five sections, each opened in red, the spell names the gods of a tribunal in a holy place (Heliopolis, Busiris, Sekhem, Pe and Dep, and the Banks of Rekhty, a place not identified) and explains a night of the story of Osiris; each section closes with a refrain asking Thoth, who made Osiris true of voice against his enemies, to make Ani true of voice before the next tribunal. Other papyri open the spell with an address to Thoth that Ani's papyrus does not have (Budge supplies it from Naville's edition), and several signs and readings in this part are doubtful.

sentences.i: As for the great tribunal which is in Heliopolis: it is Atum, Shu and Tefnut.
sentences.n: Before this, Budge prints in square brackets a passage that Ani's papyrus does not have, supplied (his note) from Naville's edition of other papyri: the opening of the spell, an address to Thoth, who makes Osiris true of voice, and the start of the section on the tribunal in Heliopolis. It is left out, so Ani's text begins with the explanation of that tribunal. This is Budge's section A, and his line numerals start again at 1 in each of the five sections A–E. The papyrus writes ir ḏꜣḏꜣt ꜥꜣt imyt iwnw in red; the gods are black. ir 'as for' is the reed and the mouth: the particle that puts a noun first as the topic, which the rest of the sentence then explains. ḏꜣḏꜣt 'tribunal' is written as in the introduction: the fire-drill ḏꜣ (coded U28, approximate) twice, a small ring with ears between them (coded W24, approximate; not read), t, a barred sign (coded N1, approximate), and the seated god and a stroke as classifiers. ꜥꜣt 'great' is the column ꜥꜣ with the arm ꜥ (printed as a low bar, coded D36) as complement and t, feminine to agree with ḏꜣḏꜣt. imyt 'which is in' is the reed, the sign im with the owl m as complement, and t: the feminine of the nisba imy. iwnw 'Heliopolis' is the pillar iwn with the pot nw (a small eared ring, coded W24, approximate) and the town sign. Each god is followed by pw, 'it is': 'Atum it is, Shu it is, Tefnut it is', a sentence without a verb that says what the topic is. tmw 'Atum' is t, the sledge tm and the chick w with the seated god; šw 'Shu' is the feather šw with w and the god; tfnwt 'Tefnut' is t, the horned viper f, a ring marked with a cross (coded W24, approximate) for nw, t, and the cobra, the classifier of goddesses. Atum is the creator god of Heliopolis, and Shu and Tefnut are the first pair he brought into being.

sentences.l: as-for · guarding · the-rebels · were-destroyed · the-confederates · of-Seth · it-is · (m) · again(?) · was-beaten(?)-he
sentences.i: As for the guarding of the rebels: it is that the confederates of Seth were destroyed when he was beaten(?) again(?).
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir sꜣyw sbiw in red. sꜣyw is a looped upright crossed by a stick (coded Aa18, approximate), the sign sꜣ, with the vulture ꜣ as complement, two reeds y and the chick w, then a low hooked sign (coded U15) and a kneeling captive with one arm bent up to his head (coded A13) with a stroke as classifiers: read as the infinitive of sꜣw 'guard, keep watch over', the captive showing what kind of guarding this is (Budge: saiu, 'fettering'). sbiw 'the rebels' is s, the foot b, the reed and the chick w, with a thin stick (coded T14, approximate) and the captive as classifiers, as in Spell 1; it follows the infinitive as its object. ḥtm·n·tw is the wick ḥ, a tall upright with a small box at its foot (coded U33, approximate) read as tm, t and the owl m as complements, a long-legged bird (coded G27, approximate) and the sparrow of bad things as classifiers, then water n, t and the chick w: taken as the sḏm·n·tw·f, the passive of the past, 'were destroyed' (Budge reads one word, ḥetem-entu, 'the destruction'). The tall sign is not identified; in Spell 17 the same place in sḥtm 'destroy' holds a tall sign coded Q1. smꜣyw 'the confederates' is the lungs and windpipe smꜣ with ꜣ, two reeds, the seated god and a stroke (Budge: sami; his footnote gives a variant ḥait). stẖ 'Seth' is the bolt s, t and a plain rectangle (coded N37, approximate) for ẖ, with the god, as in Spell 17. pw after the clause makes it the explanation: 'it is (that) …'. nm is the knife nm (coded T34, approximate; printed as a slanting wedge) with m as complement and the roll; Budge renders m nm 'the second time', and 'again' is taken from him with a query (the knife also writes nmt 'slaughter-block', which would suit the passage, but no t is written), and m is left untranslated in the literal line; this nm is not the interrogative nm 'who?'. qn·tw·f is the hill-slope q and water n with crossed sticks (coded Z9) and the sparrow as classifiers, then t, the coil w (Z7) and the viper ·f: the sḏm·tw·f, the passive, 'he was …'. The crossed sticks are the classifier of qnqn 'beat' in Spell 17, so qn is taken as 'beat, overpower'; Budge takes the clause as active, 'he wrought evil', which the tw does not allow. Both nm and qn are doubtful. The rebels are Seth's band, the murderers of Osiris, and their custody is their punishment.

sentences.l: O · Thoth · who-makes-true-of-voice · Osiris · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: O Thoth, who makes Osiris true of voice against his enemies,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i in red. This is the refrain of the spell: it closes every section, each time naming the next tribunal. i 'O' is the reed with a kneeling man with his hand at his face (coded A2) as classifier, the gesture of calling out. ḏḥwty 'Thoth' is the ibis on its standard with t and two strokes y as complements. smꜣꜥ-ḫrw is the bolt s, the sickle mꜣ, the plinth mꜣꜥ (Aa11), the oar ḫrw and the chick w, with the man with hand to mouth: the participle 'who makes true of voice' of the causative of mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice', made with s; 'to make someone true of voice' is to win his case, and the phrase is kept literal, as in Spell 1. wsir 'Osiris' is the eye over the throne with the seated god. r 'against' is the mouth, the preposition of hostility. ḫftyw·f 'his enemies' is the placenta ḫ, the viper f, t and the vulture ꜣ (an old spelling, not read; Budge: χefta), the kneeling captive (coded A13) and a stroke as classifiers, and the viper ·f; the plural ending is not written. Thoth, the god of reckoning, keeps the record at the judgement, and as he won Osiris's case against Seth before the gods, he is asked to win Ani's.

sentences.i: make the Osiris Ani true of voice against his enemies before the great tribunal which is in Busiris
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ꜣny twice, at the end of line 3 and again at the head of line 4; read it once. Budge marks the second with '(sic)'. Both writings are shown, the first with the squatting man holding a flail (A52) as classifier, the second with the kneeling man with raised arm (A1), and the second is not translated. smꜣꜥ-ḫrw is written as in the address, without the classifier: here the imperative, 'make true of voice!'. wsir ꜣny 'the Osiris Ani' names the dead man as an Osiris, the god whose case was won; the god's classifier is written as for the god. ꜣny 'Ani' is the vulture ꜣ, water n with three strokes, and two reeds y with the classifier. m 'before' is the owl, the preposition 'in', here 'in the presence of' (at the same word in the next refrain Budge's footnote gives a variant m-bꜣḥ 'before'). ḏꜣḏꜣt and ꜥꜣt as in the first unit; imyt is here the reed, the sign im and t. ḏdw 'Busiris' is the djed pillar written twice, the chick w and the town sign: Djedu, the city of Osiris in the Delta. The refrain names the tribunal that the next section explains.

sentences.n: grḥ 'night' is the jar-stand g, r and the wick ḥ with the sky and a hanging sceptre (coded N2, approximate) as classifier; it stands without a preposition, as the time when (Budge supplies '[on]'). pwy 'that' is p, w and two reeds, the demonstrative after its noun. n 'of' is water n, the genitive. sꜥḥꜥ 'setting up' is the folded cloth s and the post ꜥḥꜥ (P6) with the arm ꜥ as complement and the walking legs as classifier: the infinitive of the causative of ꜥḥꜥ 'stand', 'cause to stand'. ḏd 'the djed pillar' is the pillar itself with a stroke, the sign that is doubled in the name Djedu. m 'in' is the sign m (Aa15). sentences.i: As for the great tribunal which is in Busiris: it is Osiris, Isis, Nephthys and Horus, who protects the father.
sentences.n: Section B begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1; his footnote says that in many papyri the order of this and the following sections is changed. The papyrus writes ir ḏꜣḏꜣt ꜥꜣt imyt ḏdw in red. ꜥꜣt has t printed before the arm here. ꜣst 'Isis' is the seat ꜣs and t, with the egg (H8) and the cobra as classifiers. nbt-ḥwt 'Nephthys' is one sign, a basket on an enclosure (coded O9, approximate), with the cobra: 'Lady of the Mansion'. ḥr 'Horus' is the falcon alone. nḏ-ḥr is the sign nḏ (coded Aa27, approximate) with the pot nw (coded W24, approximate) as complement for n and a low hooked sign (U15) as classifier, then the face ḥr with its stroke: 'protect, take care of', literally 'guard the face of', as in Spell 17, here a participle, 'who protects'. itf 'the father' is t and the viper f alone, the word for father without its reed; no 'his' is written (Budge supplies it). Each name is again followed by pw. These are the family of Osiris: his sisters Isis and Nephthys, and his son Horus, who took up his cause.

sentences.n: Section C begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes ir ḏꜣḏꜣt ꜥꜣt imyt sḫm in red. ḥr-ḫnty-irty is printed by Budge as two groups, which are joined here as one name, as in Spell 17: the falcon ḥr alone, then ḫnty 'foremost' (W17, approximate) with n, t and two strokes y; then the flat sign with an upright loop (coded R22) that writes ḫm in Sekhem; then the eye twice with the seated god, irty 'the two eyes', the second eye making the dual. Budge reads the loop sign àn (Ḥeru-χenti-àn-maa); it may stand for the ḫm of Sekhem, naming the god as the one of that town, or for something else, and it is left unread. The name is taken as Horus-Khenty-irty, 'Horus Foremost of the Two Eyes', as in Spell 17, the Horus of Sekhem. ḏḥwty 'Thoth' and pw as before; one pw serves both names. nty 'who' is water n, t and two strokes y, the relative adjective, written without a plural ending; it may refer to Thoth alone, 'who is'. m 'in' is the owl, and ḏꜣḏꜣt is written as before. n-iꜣrrd-f 'En-iarered-ef' is water n, the vulture and the reed (in that order), r twice, a cord with tails (coded T12, approximate) for rd, an open box as classifier and the viper f, here without the town sign (Budge: Naàrereṭef). sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir grḥ pwy n ḫt ḫꜣwt ḥb in red. ḫꜣwt is the plant ḫꜣ (coded M12, approximate) with ꜣ, w and t, then a short stroke over a small slanting wedge (coded N21, approximate). Each 'ir' unit in this spell takes up the night named at the end of the section before (sꜥḥꜥ ḏd m ḏdw in section B, sꜥḥꜥ ꜥꜣw n ḥr in section D), and the night named at the end of section B is grḥ n ḫt ḫꜣwy m sḫm. So the word is taken as the same ḫꜣwy 'night', here written with t and without the sky classifier, as Budge reads it (χaut, 'night'). As it stands, the group could also be ḫꜣwt 'altar, offering table', as in the introduction, and the reading is doubtful. The next group, the festival bowl ḥb (W3) over the sun, has no transliteration in Budge, who renders 'of the festival': it is read ḥb 'festival', with the sun as classifier as in Spell 17; how it joins the words before it is not clear, and the reading is doubtful. ḥḏ tꜣ 'the dawn' is the mace ḥḏ (coded T3, approximate) with the cobra ḏ as complement and the sun as classifier, then the flat land sign tꜣ: literally 'the brightening of the land', daybreak. pw 'it is'. r 'at' is the mouth. qrsw 'the coffin' is the hill-slope q, r and the bolt s, with the coffin (Q6) and the low hooked sign as classifiers, its w not written. sentences.n: sꜥḥꜥ is written as in section A. ꜥꜣw is three upright columns with swelling capital and base, which match no sign exactly (coded O29, the column ꜥꜣ, approximate), written three times for a plural and read with Budge as ꜥꜣw (his āāiui, 'columns'). It has no preposition before it and is taken as a clause of time, 'when …'. n·f 'for him' is water n and the viper. iwꜥt is a young lying animal (coded E9, approximate), iw, with w as complement, the arm ꜥ and t, with the roll and a stroke: iwꜥt 'inheritance', the noun from iwꜥ 'heir' (Budge: āuāt, 'heir'; the t and the roll of abstract things point to the inheritance rather than the heir). m 'in' is the owl. ḫt 'property' is ḫ and t with the roll over plural strokes. itf·f 'his father' is t and f, father without its reed, the seated man as classifier and the viper ·f. Horus's right to his father's inheritance is what he won in his long case against Seth before the gods.

sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir sꜥḥꜥ ꜥꜣw n in red; ḥr after them is black. In sꜥḥꜥ the arm ꜥ is drawn through the foot of the post. ꜥꜣw 'pillars' (?) is the three upright columns, as in section C. ḏd 'saying' is the cobra ḏ with the hand d joined to it: the infinitive used as a noun, 'the saying of Seth', with stẖ after it as a direct genitive; stẖ is here the folded cloth s, t, the rectangle (coded N37, approximate) for ẖ and the god (Budge's footnote gives other spellings of the name). n 'to' is water n. imyw-ḫt 'the followers' is the reed, the sign im with m, w and a stroke, then the branch ḫt (M3) with ḫ and t as complements, the walking legs, and the seated man with a stroke: literally 'those who are in the following'; no 'his' is written (Budge supplies it). Then come Seth's words: sꜥḥꜥ is the imperative, 'set up!', and r·s is the mouth r with the bolt ·s, 'at it, by it'; the 'it' is feminine. The sense of the passage is not clear: the text does not say whose followers they are, or what 'it' is.

sentences.n: mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is again written without the sickle. After it stand water n and the viper, n·f 'for him, to him'; Budge renders 'is he', which n·f cannot mean. Perhaps the noun mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'vindication' is meant, with n·f, 'vindication (is) his'; perhaps the two signs are a slip. The rendering is doubtful. The place name is divided here into two words (Budge prints one group). iḏbw is three slanting wedges over three low bench-like signs, all coded N21 (approximate): the tongue of land iḏb 'bank', written three times for a plural, 'the Banks'. In Spell 1 the same sign over a canal writes iḏbwy 'the Two Banks', where the mourners of Osiris are. Budge reads the wedges Taiu(?), with his own query. rḫty is r, the placenta ḫ, t and two strokes y, then tall plants on a base (coded M20, approximate) and the town sign as classifiers (Budge: reχit). It is perhaps the place that Spell 1 writes rḫtt, Rekhtet, after the Two Banks. 'The Banks' is a fair reading of the signs, but the name and the place are not sure. The refrain names the tribunal of section E.

sentences.i: on that night when Isis lay awake, making lament for her brother Osiris.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes kꜣbyt; read iꜣkbyt 'lament'. The group is the basket k, the vulture ꜣ, the foot b, two reeds y and t, with a curled lock of hair (coded D3) and a stroke: the signs of iꜣkbyt in Spell 1, with the lock of hair that classifies mourning, but without the reed and with k before ꜣ (Budge: kabit, 'lamentation'). The word can name the mourning woman as well as the mourning; after irt 'making' it is the lament. sḏr 'lying down' is the folded cloth s, a sign of stacked bars with a hook (coded M36, approximate), ḏr, with r as complement and a figure lying on a bed (A55) as classifier: the infinitive of sḏr 'lie down, spend the night', with ꜣst 'Isis' after it as its subject. rs·ti is a sign of joined pieces of wood (coded T13, approximate), rs, with the eye as classifier, then t and w: rs 'be awake, keep watch' in the stative, the ending 'she (is)' written tw (Budge: res-tu, 'watching'). ḥr irt 'making' is the face ḥr with its stroke and the eye ir with t: ḥr with the infinitive, 'in the act of making'. The second ḥr is 'for, on account of'. sn·s 'her brother' is the arrowhead sn (coded T22) with n, the seated man as classifier and the bolt ·s. Isis's watch beside her dead brother and husband is the model of the mourning for every dead person.

sentences.n: hꜣkr 'Haker' is the reed-shelter h, the vulture ꜣ, the basket k and r, with the seated god as classifier (Budge: Haker): the name of a night festival of Osiris at Abydos, here classed as a god. m 'at' is the owl, three times. ṯnw is t, water n and the pot nw with w, then a forked upright pole (coded O30, approximate) with a bird with raised wings against it (coded G41, approximate), the roll and a stroke as classifiers: read as ṯnw, from ṯni 'be distinguished, set apart', with t for ṯ, as Spell 146 writes it, where the word also has a bird with raised wings on a post as classifier (Budge: tennu, 'separation'). It could instead be tnw 'number, count', 'the counting of the dead'; the reading is doubtful. mtw 'the dead' is the owl m, t and w with the kneeling captive (coded A13) and a stroke: the dead who are condemned, classed with enemies. sipt 'the inspecting' is the folded cloth s, the reed i, the stool p and t with the roll: the noun of sip 'inspect, check' (Budge: sàpt, 'judgment'). ꜣḫw 'the spirits' is the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ as complement, w, the squatting man with a flail (A52) and a stroke: the blessed dead. ḫpr 'the coming into being' is the scarab ḫpr with r. ihꜣbw is the reed i, the reed-shelter h, ꜣ, the foot b and w, with the man with hand to mouth (coded A2), the walking legs and plural strokes (Budge: àhabu, 'cries of joy'); the legs point to dancing and the hand at the mouth to shouting, and the word is taken as 'jubilation', with a query. tni 'Thinis' is t and water n, a tall staff hooked at the top (coded S39, approximate) taken as a classifier, two strokes y and the town sign (Budge: Teni): Teni, the old town near Abydos that the Greeks called Thinis. glossary.šw: šw — empty, lacking, free (of) (adjective; verb šwi 'be empty') · a second word of the same spelling: Shu, god of the air, who holds up the sky (god's name; Budge: Śu)
glossary.tfnwt: tfnwt — Tefnut, goddess, with her brother Shu the first pair brought forth by Atum (goddess's name; Budge: Tefnut)
glossary.sꜣw: sꜣw — Sais · a second word of the same spelling: to guard, keep watch (verb; written with the herdsman with his stick; Budge: sau) · also written with the sign sꜣ and the captive classifier, of keeping prisoners in custody (Budge: saiu)
glossary.sbiw: sbiw — rebel, the rebel serpent, enemy of the sun-god (noun m.; from sbi 'rebel'; Budge: Sebàu)
glossary.ḥtm: ḥtm — to destroy; to perish, be destroyed (verb; causative sḥtm; Budge: ḥetem)
glossary.sḏm·n·f: sḏm·n·f — the n of the sḏm·n·f, marking a completed action ("I have …", "I …ed") (verb form; written between the verb and its suffix)
glossary.sḏm·tw·f: sḏm·tw·f — the tw of the sḏm·tw·f, the passive or impersonal form ("one …", "… is done") (verb form; written after the verb, before its suffix)
glossary.smꜣyw: smꜣyw — confederates, the gang of Seth (?) (noun pl.; Budge: Sami)
glossary.stẖ: stẖ — Seth, god of storm and disorder, who murdered Osiris (god's name; written stẖ or swt; Budge: Sut)
glossary.m: m — in, from (preposition) · also "with" (instrument), "as" (m bnw "as the Bennu"), "on" (living on), "by"; im before a suffix (im·i, im·f, im·tn) · a second word of the same spelling: what? (interrogative pronoun; r m 'for what? why?') · also 'among' (with a group of people) · also the negative imperative 'do not!' (before a verb form: m irt 'do not make'; from the verb imi) · also written mꜥ, with the arm · also "of, made of" (naming the material a thing is made of) · also 'at' (of a time or event) · also 'before, in the presence of' (a god or a tribunal; like m-bꜣḥ)
glossary.nm: nm — who? (interrogative pronoun; later also written with ꜥ, nim) · m nm 'again, a second time' (?) (adverbial phrase; sense uncertain; Budge: em nem)
glossary.qn: qn — to beat, overpower (?) (verb; sense uncertain; cf. qnqn 'beat'; Budge: qen)
glossary.·f: ·f — he, him, his, it (3rd person masculine singular suffix pronoun; the horned viper)
glossary.i: i — O!, hail (the vocative interjection that opens each declaration)
glossary.ḏḥwty: ḏḥwty — Thoth, the ibis god of writing, reckoning and wisdom, recorder of the judgement of the dead (god's name; Budge: Teḥuti)
glossary.smꜣꜥ-ḫrw: smꜣꜥ-ḫrw — to make true of voice, to vindicate, justify (verb; causative of mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice'; smꜣꜥ-ḫrw N r 'vindicate N against')
glossary.wsir: wsir — Osiris, god of the dead and king of the world below; Wsir N "the Osiris N", the dead person (god's name; Budge: Àusàr)
glossary.r: r — to, towards, into, at (preposition); with an infinitive "in order to"; with the sḏmt·f "until"; after an imperative, with a suffix (ir·k), "yourself, then" · a second word of the same spelling: goose, fowl (noun; the goose sign) · also against (of hostility: r·i 'against me'); concerning, about (r·f 'concerning him')
glossary.ꜣny: ꜣny — Ani, royal scribe of Thebes, for whom the papyrus was made (personal name)
glossary.pwy: pwy — this, that (masculine demonstrative, after its noun; hrw pwy 'that day')
glossary.n: n — not; negates the verb ('I have not …') · also in n wn "there is not" · a second word of the same spelling: the preposition "to, for" (n·i "to me") · the negative also before a noun, 'without, there being no …' · the preposition also 'because of, on account of'
glossary.sꜥḥꜥ: sꜥḥꜥ — to set up, erect, make stand (verb; causative of ꜥḥꜥ 'stand'; Budge: seāḥā)
glossary.ḏd: ḏd — to say, speak (verb; ḏd in N "said by N", the formula that brings in a speech); ḏdt "words, speech" (noun from it) · a second word of the same spelling: the djed pillar, emblem of Osiris (noun m.; the pillar sign as a logogram)
glossary.ꜣst: ꜣst — Isis, wife of Osiris and mother of Horus (goddess's name, written with the seat sign; Budge: Àuset)
glossary.nbt-ḥwt: nbt-ḥwt — Nephthys, "Lady of the Mansion", sister of Isis, Osiris and Seth, a mourner of Osiris (goddess's name; Budge: Nebt-ḥet)
glossary.ḥr: ḥr — face; (preposition) upon, on, over, concerning · a second word of the same spelling: Horus, the falcon god, son of Osiris and Isis; the sun as a falcon (god's name; Budge: Ḥeru) · also 'at' (ḥr sbꜣw 'at the gates'); ḥr-tp 'upon' (compound preposition: ḥr + tp 'head') · also for, on behalf of; on account of (preposition; ḥr·k 'for you')
glossary.nḏ: nḏ — to protect, guard (verb) · in the compound nḏ-ḥr 'to protect, take care of' (verb; with ḥr 'face')
glossary.itf: itf — father (noun m.; plural itw 'fathers, forefathers')
glossary.qꜥḥ: qꜥḥ — shoulder, perhaps arm (noun; Budge: qāḥ; exact sense uncertain)
glossary.ḫnty: ḫnty — foremost, who is at the head of (nisba adjective; ḫnty imntt "Foremost of the West", a title of Osiris) · a second word of the same spelling: a pigment or colour (noun; reading doubtful)
glossary.sḫm: sḫm — power, might; sacred image, cult statue (noun) · also the verb 'prevail, have power (over: m)' (sḫm m 'have power over') · also Sekhem, Letopolis, a city of Horus north of Memphis (place name; Budge: Seχem)
glossary.iw: iw — opens a statement, often with a suffix (iw·f "he …"); not translated (particle)
glossary.·sn: ·sn — they, them, their (3rd person plural suffix pronoun)
glossary.ḥꜣ: ḥꜣ — behind, around, about (preposition; Budge: ḥa)
glossary.mrw: mrw — bandages (?) (noun, plural; perhaps from mr 'bind'; sense uncertain; Budge: meru)
glossary.mꜣꜥ-ḫrw: mꜣꜥ-ḫrw — true of voice, vindicated (epithet; said of the dead whose words were found true at the judgement) · also, as a noun, vindication, the being found true (m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'in vindication'; written in full or short)
glossary.ḫt: ḫt — thing, things, property (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: wood, tree, stick, a wooden board (noun m.) · a third word: stairway, terrace (?) (noun; written with the stairway sign; Budge: χet, 'steps') · a fourth word: rear, following (noun; m-ḫt 'after', imyw-ḫt 'those in the following of') · a fifth word: fire, flame (noun; written with the flame as classifier; Budge: χet) · also a rod as a measure of length (?) (noun; Budge: χet)
glossary.ḫꜣwy: ḫꜣwy — evening, night (noun) · also written ḫꜣwt, with t (?)
glossary.ḥr-ḫnty-irty: ḥr-ḫnty-irty — Horus-Khenty-irty, 'Horus Foremost of the Two Eyes', a form of Horus (god's name; Budge: Ḥeru-khenti-maa)
glossary.nty: nty — who, which, that (relative adjective); as a noun "he who"
glossary.n-iꜣrrd-f: n-iꜣrrd-f — En-iarered-ef, a holy place of Osiris; the name looks like n rd·f "it does not grow" (?) (place name; reading uncertain; Budge: Àn-àarruṭ-f)
glossary.ḥḏ: ḥḏ — to damage, defraud, diminish · a second word of the same spelling: white, bright (adjective; verb 'be white, bright'; written with the mace)
glossary.tꜣ: tꜣ — to be hot; tꜣ-ib 'hot-tempered' · a second word of the same spelling: land, earth (noun; plural tꜣw 'lands'; dual tꜣwy 'the Two Lands', Egypt; tp tꜣ 'upon earth')
glossary.qrsw: qrsw — coffin (noun m.; the w often not written; cf. qrs 'to bury'; Budge: qeres)
glossary.sš: sš — scribe (noun; the palette-and-pen sign) · a second word of the same spelling: to pass, go through (verb; doubtful here) · also to write, draw, paint (verb; written with the scribe's palette) · also the noun 'writing, document, record' (noun m.) · also to open (a door), spread open (verb; said of doors and bolts) · a further word of the same spelling: nest (noun m.; written with the nest of young birds; dual sšwy)
glossary.p: p — Pe, with Dep one of the twin towns of Buto in the north-western Delta, an old seat of Horus (place name; written pt; Budge: Pet)
glossary.dp: dp — Dep, with Pe one of the twin towns of Buto in the north-western Delta, an old seat of Horus (place name; written dpt; Budge: Ṭept)
glossary.ꜥꜣw: ꜥꜣw — pillars, columns (?) (noun m. plural; written with the column sign three times; reading uncertain, perhaps iwnw 'pillars'; Budge: āāiui)
glossary.smn: smn — to make firm, establish (verb; causative of mn 'be firm'; Budge: smen)
glossary.iwꜥt: iwꜥt — inheritance (noun f.; from iwꜥ 'heir'; Budge: āuāt)
glossary.imsty: imsty — Imsety, one of the four sons of Horus, who guard the dead man's inner organs (god's name; also written msṯi; Budge: Mesthà)
glossary.ḥpy: ḥpy — Hapy, one of the four sons of Horus (god's name; not the Nile flood ḥꜥpy; Budge: Ḥāpi)
glossary.·s: ·s — she, her, it, its (3rd person feminine singular suffix pronoun; the folded cloth or the bolt)
glossary.iḏb: iḏb — bank, riverbank, shore (noun m.); dual iḏbwy 'the Two Banks' (Egypt, or the Nile's two sides) · plural iḏbw 'banks' (the sign written three times)
glossary.rḫtt: rḫtt — a place name, not identified (Budge: Reχtet; meaning uncertain) · perhaps also written rḫty (?), in iḏbw rḫty 'the Banks of Rekhty' (Budge: reχit)
glossary.sḏr: sḏr — to lie down, spend the night (verb; Budge: st'er)
glossary.rs: rs — to be awake, keep watch (verb; Budge: res)
glossary.·ti: ·ti — you (2nd person singular ending of the stative: "you are …, you have …"; written ·tw here) · also written ·ṯi, with the tethering rope ṯ and the reed (the older spelling) · also 3rd person feminine singular ending of the stative: 'she, it is …' (written ·ṯi, as in sšw·ṯi 'it is emptied') · the 3rd feminine singular ending also written ·tw (rs·ti 'she is awake')
glossary.iꜣkb: iꜣkb — to mourn, wail (verb); iꜣkbyt 'wailing woman, mourner' (noun f.) · also iꜣkbyt 'lament, mourning' (noun f.; irt iꜣkbyt 'make lament')
glossary.sn: sn — two (numeral; sp sn 'twice', written after a word to be said twice) · a second word of the same spelling: brother; companion, fellow (noun m.) · a third word of the same spelling: them, they (3rd person plural dependent pronoun; object of a verb, or subject after a particle)
glossary.ḥtp: ḥtp — to be content, at peace, to rest (verb); peace; offering (noun; m ḥtp "in peace")
glossary.ꜣbḏw: ꜣbḏw — Abydos, the holy city of Osiris (place name; Budge: Àbṭu) · a second word of the same spelling: the abdju-fish (noun; a fish that swims before the sun's bark)
glossary.hꜣkr: hꜣkr — Haker, a night festival of Osiris at Abydos (name of a festival, which may take the god's classifier; Budge: Haker)
glossary.ṯni: ṯni — to be distinguished, raised above (verb); ṯnw, greatness (?) (noun; Budge: θennu) · also ṯnw 'distinguishing, setting apart' (?) (infinitive; written with t; Budge: tennu)
glossary.mt: mt — a dead man (noun m.; plural mtw 'the dead', often the condemned dead, with the classifier of enemies; Budge: mitu)
glossary.sip: sip — to inspect, check, examine (verb; Budge: sàpu)
glossary.ꜣḫ: ꜣḫ — spirit, the glorified and effective dead (noun; written with the crested ibis) · also glory, effective power (noun m.) · also glorious, effective (adjective) · also to be glorious, be effective, be an effective spirit (verb) · also ꜣḫt, what is effective or useful, a benefit (noun f.) · also ꜣḫ n, to be of use to, serve, benefit (someone) (verb)
glossary.ḫpr: ḫpr — to come into being, happen, become (verb)
glossary.ihꜣbw: ihꜣbw — jubilation, rejoicing (?) (noun; sense uncertain; Budge: àhabu)
glossary.tni: tni — Teni, Thinis, the old town near Abydos (place name; Budge: Teni)
